stem: The grass *Oryza sativa* is grown as a food crop to produce rice. Rice plants are adapted to grow with their roots submerged in water.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
• 10-day old seedlings were grown with their roots submerged in water.
• Some were grown in water that was kept oxygenated and others were grown in water that did not contain oxygen (deoxygenated).
• At 12 hour intervals, some seedlings from each group were removed and transverse sections of their roots were prepared and examined.
• The sections were cut at the same distances from the root tip to check for development.
• The percentage of root tissue that had developed into aerenchyma tissue was calculated.

The results are shown in Fig. 7.1.
{{figure:figure_7_1.webp}}
Fig. 7.1
parts.text: An experiment was carried out to investigate the development of aerenchyma tissue in the roots of rice plants.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Describe the results shown in Fig. 7.1.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Describe the structure of aerenchyma **and** explain how this is an adaptation that allows roots of rice plants to be submerged in water.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe **and** explain **two** other adaptations of rice plants to growing in flooded fields.
